title: Staying with a child’s body: presence, pause, and the right not to perform

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source and seed-brief synthesis for rev0019 pediatric/perinatal high-gate architecture; no private testimony, no child words, no photographs, no public rendering.
source_packet.collection_method: manual public-source extraction, source-card routing, seed-cue factoring, and high-gate audit/refactor during rev0019
limitations: Public sources support orientation, vocabulary, and review routing only; they do not supply consented pediatric or perinatal bedside detail.
Pediatric and perinatal material is highest-gate because it can expose children, siblings, bereaved parents, photographs, school communities, and living families.
Records must not advise clinical care, child disclosure, memory-making choices, school crisis response, legal/reporting steps, or suicide/investigation handling.

moment.plain_scene: After a child dies, some families stay, hold, wash, dress, speak, pray, take photos, or pause; others cannot or choose not to. The moment is both body care and family rupture.
ordinary_language_queries: child body after death memory making

content_layers.observation_text: After a child dies, some families stay, hold, wash, dress, speak, pray, take photos, or pause; others cannot or choose not to. The moment is both body care and family rupture.
content_layers.source_synthesis: Child Bereavement UK, RCH, and sibling/end-of-life sources support family presence and memory-making possibilities, but the exact practices are setting-, family-, and culture-dependent.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: For DeathVocab, pediatric/perinatal material must be architected before it is narrated: the archive can name the kind of room, but it has not earned the right to publish a child’s words, a sibling’s memory, a baby’s image, or a parent’s fresh account.
interpretation.public_rendering_rule: Render, if ever, as guarded orientation and vocabulary only; never as clinical advice, parenting instruction, grief performance, school protocol, investigation advice, or spectacle.

what_this_is_not: not permission to publish a child’s words, drawings, photographs, or family details
uncertainties: Public sources cannot provide the room texture that consented accounts might provide later.
Age, development, diagnosis, culture, disability, language, family structure, setting, law, and timing may change what is appropriate.
The archive has not field-tested a child-material consent and review process.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay route should not imply that a family must stay, hold, wash, photograph, or perform grief correctly.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: Practitioner review must separate what is possible, what is offered, what is chosen, and what is culturally or legally constrained.
language_notes: Use concrete language without forcing a single developmental rule or script.
Do not treat the parent, child, sibling, clinician, chaplain, school, or institution as the sole authority over the whole event.
Keep memory-making, photographs, body details, and child utterances behind explicit consent and specialist review.

provenance.provenance_statement: Added in rev0019 from public-source synthesis and seed-cue factoring; no private account, no child material, no photographs, no clinical validation, no legal validation, no public release.

safety.identifiability_boundary: Do not admit names, photographs, rare diagnoses, school/community details, sibling quotes, child drawings, exact timelines, or distinctive family details without exceptional consent and harm review.
safety.medical_advice_risk: Do not use this record to decide symptoms, medications, resuscitation, hospice, transfers, feeding, hydration, ventilation, neonatal care, or place of death.
safety.legal_or_facility_advice_risk: Do not infer parental authority, reporting duties, death investigation steps, school obligations, certification, documentation, disposition, or jurisdictional definitions from this record.
safety.cultural_or_ritual_risk: Do not generalize perinatal, child, family, or religious practices into rules; route tradition-specific material to tradition-holder and cultural-safety review.
safety.clinical_boundary: This is not clinical advice or a substitute for the local pediatric, perinatal, neonatal, hospice, palliative, emergency, bereavement, school, or public-health team.
safety_notes: Many child and perinatal materials may remain permanently unpublished even if they are archiveable.
Public sources are not consent for private family stories or images.
Avoid making memory-making, honesty, sibling inclusion, or place-of-death choices into moral tests.
